The Derivative of the Coefficient Hessian in the Hyperparameters

Source: R/marginal_derivatives.R
penalty_dhessian.Rd

\(\partial S/\partial\theta_m = \partial^3\rho/\partial\beta^2\, \partial\theta_m\), one matrix per hyperparameter.

Usage

penalty_dhessian(pen, beta, theta, ...)

Arguments

pen

A penalty object.

beta

A numeric vector of coefficients.

theta

A named list of hyperparameters.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A named list of matrices, one per hyperparameter.

Details

penalty_hessian says how curved the penalty is in the coefficients; this says how that curvature moves with each hyperparameter. It is the piece a marginal criterion needs to differentiate \(\log|H+S|\).

Every branch answers in closed form. For quadratic_penalty the Hessian is \(\lambda D'PD\) and the derivative is \(D'PD\); for additive_penalty it is the component \(P_k\) of each smoothing parameter; for structured_penalty it is the matrix parameter's own param_d1; for distrib_penalty it is \(-D'\mathrm{diag}(\partial^3\ell/\partial y^2\partial\theta_m)D\), which distributions7 supplies as distrib_cross2_y. A penalty defined by its derivative rather than by a density – scad_penalty, mcp_penalty – has no such quantity where its kinks are and rejects.

See also

penalty_hessian, penalty_d2hessian, penalty_dcross

Examples

pen <- quadratic_penalty(diag(3))
penalty_dhessian(pen, c(1, 2, 3), list(lambda = 2))
#> $lambda
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    1    0    0
#> [2,]    0    1    0
#> [3,]    0    0    1
#>
